findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the catalog database will accept unencrypted client connections. Data in transit between the application server and the database can travel in cleartext.

The database password (var.password) and username are interpolated directly into the EC2 user_data script, which is stored unencrypted in the instance metadata service and readable by any process or user on the instance, as well as by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute permissions. It is also rendered in plaintext in Terraform state and plan output.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with an attached IAM instance profile (catalog_app_profile) and a public-facing web application (PHP index.php), this exposes the instance to SSRF-based credential theft of the role's temporary credentials.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device block with encrypted = true is declared, so the instance's root volume may be created without EBS encryption at rest, leaving the database credential file (/var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) and application data unencrypted on disk.

The bootstrap script installs and starts httpd serving the application over plain HTTP with no TLS configuration, so form-submitted personal data (NAME, ADDRESS) and any session data traverse the network in cleartext.

The instance is placed in a subnet (portal_subnet_a) and the file exports an output catalog_app_public_dns, indicating the instance receives a public DNS name and is reachable from the internet, directly exposing the PHP application and its attached IAM role to untrusted networks.
storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so the MySQL database volume and its snapshots store catalog data in cleartext on disk, with no KMS protection.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the MySQL listener to untrusted networks and relying solely on the security group as a boundary.

The master username is hard-coded to the privileged 'admin' account and the password is supplied via a plain Terraform variable (var.password), which is recorded in cleartext in Terraform state and is likely to be committed or passed insecurely rather than sourced from Secrets Manager.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the EC2 instance role full control over all buckets, instances and databases in the account. Because this role is attached (via aws_iam_instance_profile.catalog_app_profile) to an internet-facing app server, compromise of that host yields near account-wide privileges including privilege escalation and data exfiltration.

Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, providing an unconstrained outbound channel that facilitates data exfiltration or command-and-control if the database host is compromised.

No parameter enforcing TLS (e.g. require_secure_transport) is applied and the referenced parameter group is not shown, so client connections to the publicly accessible MySQL endpoint may occur in cleartext.
